caption: R10 650 of my salary goes to people I owe before I buy a loaf of bread. How long did yours take?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R32 000
p/m salary
Living in Polokwane
slides.body:
Female, 38
Divorced, one child at home
Job: High school teacher
Net salary: R32 000 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: I moved here for the school run, not the address. It's ten minutes from the gate.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: 27 months left on paper. It is the biggest single thing I owe and the one I can't sell my way out of.

slides.title: Credit card
slides.body: About 11 months if I don't touch it again. I've said that before.

slides.title: Personal loan
slides.includes: R48 000 balance, 24% interest, 24 months to go
slides.body: I took it to cover my mother's hospital bill in 2023. I don't regret it. I do watch the interest.

slides.title: Takeaways & tuckshop coffee
slides.includes: Staffroom lunches, Friday chicken, delivery on report weeks
slides.body: I would have guessed R600. It is R1 700. That's the number I'm not proud of.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Groceries, petrol & insurance, home running costs, medical aid, black tax, store accounts, funeral policy
slides.body: R12 700 that isn't debt and isn't rent. It's the only part I can actually move if a month goes wrong.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R32 000. R10 650 of that went to R180 000 of debt — card, loan, store accounts, car. On this pace the accounts clear in 8 months, the card in 11, the loan in 24, the car in 27.

slides.title: I stopped guessing what I owe
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

Seeing the four debt repayments added up on one screen was worse, and more useful, than any of them alone.

No bank login needed.
